1	# Business Requirements Document: Credit Control
2	
3	| | |
4	|---|---|
5	| Prepared for | Finance Director |
6	| Prepared by | Business Analyst, Finance |
7	| Version | 1.0 (draft for sign-off) |
8	| Status | For review by Finance, Sales and IT |
9	
10	## 1. Purpose
11	
12	This document sets out what the business needs from a credit control capability in our ERP system. Today credit control lives in a spreadsheet and in the head of our credit controller. The board has asked that it move into the ERP, so that the same rules are applied to every customer every time, so that sales staff and customers cannot get around them, and so that our auditors can see what was decided, by whom and when.
13	
14	The document describes the business behaviour we want. It does not say how the software should be built.
15	
16	## 2. Background
17	
18	We are a wholesale distributor with about 900 trade customers on account. Customers are billed in several currencies. Orders reach us in four main ways: entered by our sales office, placed by customers through our web shop, sent to us electronically by larger customers, and raised automatically from standing monthly orders.
19	
20	Last financial year our bad debt write-offs were well above what the board considers acceptable. A review found the main causes were:
21	
22	- Customers kept being supplied after they had stopped paying, because the "stop list" was a spreadsheet that the sales office and the web shop did not check.
23	- Credit limits were set once when the account was opened and rarely looked at again.
24	- Reminder letters were sent irregularly, depending on how busy the credit controller was.
25	- We charged no interest or late fees, so slow payers had no reason to pay on time.
26	- Write-offs were posted inconsistently, and at year end the auditors had trouble matching the sales ledger to the general ledger and to the decisions behind each write-off.
27	
28	We already use the ERP for sales orders, invoicing, customer accounts, statements and the general ledger, so the credit control work should sit there too.
29	
30	## 3. Stakeholders
31	
32	| Stakeholder | Interest |
33	|---|---|
34	| Finance Director (sponsor) | Lower bad debt, consistent control, a clean audit. |
35	| Maria, Credit Controller | Runs credit control day to day: reviews, stops, reminders, charges, write-offs. |
36	| Deputy Credit Controller | Covers for Maria with the same authority. |
37	| Financial Accountant | Month-end close; the ledger must agree with customer accounts. |
38	| Sales Manager and sales reps | Need to know which of their customers are on stop or on watch; must not be able to override it. |
39	| Sales office / order entry | Must be stopped from processing orders for customers on stop. |
40	| Customers | See their own reminders, interest and fees; receive reminder letters by email. |
41	| External auditors | Need a trail of credit decisions, charges and write-offs. |
42	| IT / system administrator | Installs and configures the change on our live system. |
43	
44	## 4. Scope
45	
46	### 4.1 In scope
47	
48	1. Periodic credit reviews of customers, recording the outcome, notes and the next review date.
49	2. Putting customers "on stop" (also called "on hold" or "frozen") and taking them off stop.
50	3. A softer "watch" status for customers we are worried about but still supply.
51	4. Overdue reminder letters ("chasers", "dunning letters") in escalating stages, sent by email.
52	5. Interest and/or late fees on overdue balances, charged at month end.
53	6. Writing off bad debts.
54	7. A report of customers due a credit review and customers over their credit limit.
55	8. Sales reps seeing only their own customers' credit information.
56	9. Customers seeing their own reminders and charges in the customer portal.
57	10. Month-end agreement between the general ledger and customer accounts.
58	11. Working on both our existing live system and on any new installation.
59	12. Updating the staff guide.
60	
61	### 4.2 Out of scope
62	
63	- Credit insurance and external credit-reference agency feeds.
64	- Debt collection agencies and legal proceedings (we will continue to handle these outside the system, though we want a note of them against the customer).
65	- Changes to how customers pay us, or to cash allocation.
66	- Customer credit applications and account opening.
67	- Supplier (purchase ledger) side.
68	- Changes to price lists, discounts or sales commissions.
69	
70	## 5. Business Requirements
71	
72	### 5.1 Credit reviews
73	
74	- **BR-01** Credit control must be able to record a credit review against any customer. A review records the date, who did it, the outcome (for example: limit confirmed, limit raised, limit reduced, put on watch, put on stop), any new credit limit, free-text notes and the next review date.
75	- **BR-02** Every customer on account must have a next review date. New customers get one automatically when their account is opened, based on a standard review period set by Finance (we expect 12 months, and shorter for higher-risk customers).
76	- **BR-03** The full history of reviews for a customer must be kept and viewable. Past reviews cannot be changed or deleted.
77	- **BR-04** When a review changes the credit limit, the customer's limit must update as part of the review, so the limit and the reason for it are always recorded together.
78	
79	### 5.2 Stop and watch
80	
81	- **BR-05** Credit control must be able to put a customer on stop, with a reason, and take them off stop, with a reason. Each change records who did it and when.
82	- **BR-06** While a customer is on stop, no new orders may be accepted or released for them, by any route: the sales office, the web shop, electronic orders and standing monthly orders. Goods must not be dispatched or invoiced on existing orders taken before the stop, unless credit control releases them.
83	- **BR-07** Only the credit controller and the deputy (and the Finance Director) may put customers on or off stop, or change credit limits. Sales reps and sales office staff must not be able to.
84	- **BR-08** Credit control must be able to put a customer on "watch". A customer on watch can still be supplied, but anyone taking an order for them must be clearly warned, and credit control should be able to see orders taken for watched customers.
85	- **BR-09** A customer's credit status (normal, watch or on stop) must be clearly visible wherever staff look at that customer or take an order for them.
86	- **BR-10** Orders that would take a customer over their credit limit must be held for credit control's approval rather than accepted outright. (Today reps "just put it through".)
87	- **BR-11** Where a customer has asked for or been told about a stop, the customer should see in the web shop that their account is on hold and should contact us, rather than having orders silently fail.
88	
89	### 5.3 Reminder letters (dunning)
90	
91	- **BR-12** The system must send overdue reminder letters in escalating stages. We expect three stages to start with: a polite reminder, a firmer second letter, and a final notice warning that the account will be put on stop and charges applied. Finance must be able to set the number of stages, how many days overdue triggers each stage and the wording of each letter.
92	- **BR-13** Reminders must go by email to the customer's accounts contact. Customers with no email address must be listed so that credit control can post the letter.
93	- **BR-14** Reminders are produced in a regular run (we expect weekly) started by credit control. Before sending, credit control must be able to see who will get which letter and leave out particular customers (for example, where a payment has been promised or there is a dispute).
94	- **BR-15** A customer should only move up a stage if they are still overdue; a customer who pays must not get the next letter. A customer must not receive the same stage twice in a short time.
95	- **BR-16** Every reminder sent must be recorded against the customer: the date, the stage, what invoices it covered and the amount.
96	- **BR-17** Reminders must be in the customer's own currency and show their overdue invoices.
97	- **BR-18** Credit control should be able to mark an invoice as disputed, so that it is not chased and not charged interest until the dispute is settled.
98	
99	### 5.4 Interest and late fees
100	
101	- **BR-19** At month end the system must be able to charge interest on overdue balances, a fixed late fee, or both. Finance must be able to set the interest rate, the fee amount and how many days overdue a balance must be before it is charged.
102	- **BR-20** It must be possible to exempt individual customers from interest and/or fees (for example, key accounts or those with agreed payment plans).
103	- **BR-21** Charges must be raised in the customer's own currency and must appear on the customer's account and their next statement as separate, clearly described items.
104	- **BR-22** Before charges are posted, credit control must be able to see a list of what will be charged to whom, and confirm it. The same month must not be charged twice.
105	- **BR-23** Interest and fees must post to the general ledger to the income accounts that Finance chooses.
106	- **BR-24** Credit control must be able to waive (reverse) a charge for a customer, with a reason, and the reversal must also reach the ledger.
107	
108	### 5.5 Bad debt write-off
109	
110	- **BR-25** Credit control must be able to write off all or part of a customer's unpaid balance as a bad debt, with a reason.
111	- **BR-26** Write-offs above an amount set by Finance must be approved by the Finance Director before they take effect.
112	- **BR-27** A write-off must reduce the customer's balance and post to the bad debt account in the general ledger, including any currency difference.
113	- **BR-28** When a customer has a debt written off, the customer should be put on stop automatically, unless credit control decides otherwise.
114	- **BR-29** There must be a report of write-offs over a period, showing customer, amount, reason, who did it and who approved it.
115	
116	### 5.6 Reporting
117	
118	- **BR-30** A credit control report must list customers who are due or overdue for a credit review, customers over their credit limit (and by how much), and customers on watch or on stop. It must be filterable by sales rep and by currency, and totals must be shown in our home currency.
119	- **BR-31** The aged debt report must show each customer's credit status, credit limit and the last reminder stage sent.
120	- **BR-32** All credit control actions (reviews, stop/watch changes, limit changes, reminders, charges, waivers and write-offs) must be visible as a history per customer that the auditors can inspect.
121	
122	### 5.7 Sales reps
123	
124	- **BR-33** Sales reps must see credit information (status, limit, balance, overdue amounts, reminders) only for their own customers, not for other reps' customers.
125	- **BR-34** Reps can see but not change credit status or limits.
126	
127	### 5.8 Customer portal
128	
129	- **BR-35** Customers who log in to the portal must be able to see the reminder letters we have sent them and the interest and fees charged to their account, along with their balance.
130	- **BR-36** A customer must only ever see their own account.
131	
132	### 5.9 Month end and the ledger
133	
134	- **BR-37** At month end the total of all customer balances must agree with the trade debtors control account in the general ledger, after interest, fees, waivers and write-offs have been posted.
135	- **BR-38** If they do not agree, Finance must be able to find out why from the system.
136	
137	### 5.10 Installation and rollout
138	
139	- **BR-39** The capability must work on our existing live system, with all our existing customers, balances and history, as well as on a brand-new installation.
140	- **BR-40** On go-live every existing customer starts as "normal", with a next review date set by Finance, unless credit control loads their current status from the spreadsheet. Existing customers who are on the spreadsheet stop list today must be on stop in the system from day one.
141	- **BR-41** Nothing in the new capability should change how existing invoices, statements or postings behave for customers who are not overdue.
142	
143	### 5.11 Documentation and training
144	
145	- **BR-42** The staff guide must be updated to explain credit reviews, stop and watch, the reminder run, month-end charges, write-offs and the credit control report.
146	- **BR-43** Sales staff need a short note on what "watch" and "stop" mean for them and who to contact.
147	
148	## 6. User Stories
149	
150	1. **As Maria (credit controller)**, I want to see every Monday which customers are due a review or over their limit, so that I can work through them in order and nothing slips.
151	2. **As Maria**, I want to put a customer on stop once, and know that the sales office, the web shop, EDI orders and the standing orders are all blocked, so that I don't have to phone round.
152	3. **As the deputy credit controller**, I want the same powers and the same history as Maria, so that I can cover her holidays without asking her what she agreed with whom.
153	4. **As a sales rep**, I want to see when one of my customers is on watch or on stop, and why, so that I can talk to the customer before they place an order.
154	5. **As Maria**, I want the weekly reminder run to email the right letter at the right stage to each overdue customer, after I've had a chance to take out the ones I'm already talking to.
155	6. **As the Financial Accountant**, I want month-end interest and fees to post themselves to the ledger, so that the debtors control account agrees with the customer balances without manual journals.
156	7. **As the Finance Director**, I want to approve large write-offs before they go through, so that I know what bad debt we are taking.
157	8. **As a customer**, I want to see in the portal the reminders and charges on my account, so that I understand what I owe and why.
158	9. **As the external auditor**, I want to see for any customer who changed their credit limit or status, when and why, so that I can test the credit control process.
159	
160	## 7. Acceptance Criteria (business terms)
161	
162	- **AC-01** Maria records a review on a customer, raising their limit and setting next review in six months. The new limit applies straight away, and the review, with her notes, appears in the customer's history. The customer drops off the "due for review" list and reappears when the next date comes round.
163	- **AC-02** A customer is put on stop. An order for them cannot be completed in the sales office, through the web shop, electronically or from their standing order. When they are taken off stop, orders go through again. Both changes appear in their history with reasons.
164	- **AC-03** A sales rep tries to take a customer off stop or raise a limit and cannot.
165	- **AC-04** A customer on watch places an order: it is accepted, the person taking it sees a warning, and the order shows on credit control's list.
166	- **AC-05** An order that would take a customer over their limit is held and only released when credit control approves it.
167	- **AC-06** In the reminder run, a customer 35 days overdue gets the first letter by email; the next run, if still unpaid and past the second threshold, they get the second letter; if they pay in between, they get nothing. A customer marked disputed gets no letter. Every letter sent shows on the customer's account history and in their portal.
168	- **AC-07** At month end, an overdue customer is charged interest at the set rate and the set late fee in their own currency; an exempt customer is not charged; running the charges again for the same month charges nobody twice. The charges appear on the customer's statement and in the portal.
169	- **AC-08** After month-end charges, waivers and write-offs, the total of customer balances equals the debtors control account in the general ledger.
170	- **AC-09** A write-off below the approval amount reduces the customer's balance and appears in the bad debt account; one above it does nothing until the Finance Director approves it. The customer is put on stop.
171	- **AC-10** Rep A sees credit details for her customers and none for Rep B's customers. Customer X in the portal sees only Customer X's reminders and charges.
172	- **AC-11** After go-live on the live system, all existing customers, balances and history are intact, every customer has a next review date, and everyone on the old spreadsheet stop list is on stop.
173	- **AC-12** The updated staff guide covers every item in section 4.1 and has been read and agreed by Maria and the Sales Manager.
174	
175	## 8. Assumptions
176	
177	- Customers' accounts contact email addresses are mostly up to date; credit control will clean up the rest before go-live.
178	- Each customer already has a single sales rep assigned.
179	- Our terms and conditions allow us to charge interest and late fees; Legal will confirm the wording for letters.
180	- Credit control will provide the current stop list and credit limits from the spreadsheet for go-live.
181	
182	## 9. Open Questions
183	
184	1. Interest: a simple annual rate on overdue balances, or a statutory late-payment rate? Does it differ by currency or country?
185	2. Late fee: one flat fee per month, or a fee per overdue invoice? Should it vary by currency?
186	3. Do we charge interest on interest and fees that are themselves overdue?
187	4. Should a customer be put on stop automatically after the final reminder, or only flagged for Maria to decide?
188	5. How should over-limit orders from the web shop and standing orders be handled: held for approval, or rejected with a message to the customer?
189	6. What is the approval threshold for write-offs, and does the Financial Accountant also need to sign off?
190	7. If a written-off debt is later paid, how do we want it shown?
191	8. Should reps be told the reason for a stop, or only that the customer is on stop?
192	9. Do we need the reminder letters in languages other than English for overseas customers?
193	10. Should customers be able to see "watch" status in the portal? (Our view: no.)
194	11. Who covers credit decisions when both Maria and her deputy are away?
195	12. Do head-office/branch customer groups share one credit limit, or does each branch have its own?

Goods must not be dispatched or invoiced on existing orders taken before the stop, unless credit control releases them.
- **BR-07** Only the credit controller and the deputy (and the Finance Director) may put customers on or off stop, or change credit limits. Sales reps and sales office staff must not be able to.
- **BR-08** Credit control must be able to put a customer on "watch". A customer on watch can still be supplied, but anyone taking an order for them must be clearly warned, and credit control should be able to see orders taken for watched customers.
- **BR-09** A customer's credit status (normal, watch or on stop) must be clearly visible wherever staff look at that customer or take an order for them.
- **BR-10** Orders that would take a customer over their credit limit must be held for credit control's approval rather than accepted outright. (Today reps "just put it through".)
- **BR-11** Where a customer has asked for or been told about a stop, the customer should see in the web shop that their account is on hold and should contact us, rather than having orders silently fail.

### 5.3 Reminder letters (dunning)

- **BR-12** The system must send overdue reminder letters in escalating stages. We expect three stages to start with: a polite reminder, a firmer second letter, and a final notice warning that the account will be put on stop and charges applied. Finance must be able to set the number of stages, how many days overdue triggers each stage and the wording of each letter.
- **BR-13** Reminders must go by email to the customer's accounts contact. Customers with no email address must be listed so that credit control can post the letter.
- **BR-14** Reminders are produced in a regular run (we expect weekly) started by credit control. Before sending, credit control must be able to see who will get which letter and leave out particular customers (for example, where a payment has been promised or there is a dispute).
- **BR-15** A customer should only move up a stage if they are still overdue; a customer who pays must not get the next letter. A customer must not receive the same stage twice in a short time.
- **BR-16** Every reminder sent must be recorded against the customer: the date, the stage, what invoices it covered and the amount.
- **BR-17** Reminders must be in the customer's own currency and show their overdue invoices.
- **BR-18** Credit control should be able to mark an invoice as disputed, so that it is not chased and not charged interest until the dispute is settled.

### 5.4 Interest and late fees

- **BR-19** At month end the system must be able to charge interest on overdue balances, a fixed late fee, or both. Finance must be able to set the interest rate, the fee amount and how many days overdue a balance must be before it is charged.
- **BR-20** It must be possible to exempt individual customers from interest and/or fees (for example, key accounts or those with agreed payment plans).
- **BR-21** Charges must be raised in the customer's own currency and must appear on the customer's account and their next statement as separate, clearly described items.
- **BR-22** Before charges are posted, credit control must be able to see a list of what will be charged to whom, and confirm it. The same month must not be charged twice.
- **BR-23** Interest and fees must post to the general ledger to the income accounts that Finance chooses.
- **BR-24** Credit control must be able to waive (reverse) a charge for a customer, with a reason, and the reversal must also reach the ledger.

### 5.5 Bad debt write-off

- **BR-25** Credit control must be able to write off all or part of a customer's unpaid balance as a bad debt, with a reason.
- **BR-26** Write-offs above an amount set by Finance must be approved by the Finance Director before they take effect.
- **BR-27** A write-off must reduce the customer's balance and post to the bad debt account in the general ledger, including any currency difference.
- **BR-28** When a customer has a debt written off, the customer should be put on stop automatically, unless credit control decides otherwise.
- **BR-29** There must be a report of write-offs over a period, showing customer, amount, reason, who did it and who approved it.

### 5.6 Reporting

- **BR-30** A credit control report must list customers who are due or overdue for a credit review, customers over their credit limit (and by how much), and customers on watch or on stop. It must be filterable by sales rep and by currency, and totals must be shown in our home currency.
- **BR-31** The aged debt report must show each customer's credit status, credit limit and the last reminder stage sent.
- **BR-32** All credit control actions (reviews, stop/watch changes, limit changes, reminders, charges, waivers and write-offs) must be visible as a history per customer that the auditors can inspect.

### 5.7 Sales reps

- **BR-33** Sales reps must see credit information (status, limit, balance, overdue amounts, reminders) only for their own customers, not for other reps' customers.
- **BR-34** Reps can see but not change credit status or limits.

### 5.8 Customer portal

- **BR-35** Customers who log in to the portal must be able to see the reminder letters we have sent them and the interest and fees charged to their account, along with their balance.
- **BR-36** A customer must only ever see their own account.

### 5.9 Month end and the ledger

- **BR-37** At month end the total of all customer balances must agree with the trade debtors control account in the general ledger, after interest, fees, waivers and write-offs have been posted.
- **BR-38** If they do not agree, Finance must be able to find out why from the system.

### 5.10 Installation and rollout

- **BR-39** The capability must work on our existing live system, with all our existing customers, balances and history, as well as on a brand-new installation.
- **BR-40** On go-live every existing customer starts as "normal", with a next review date set by Finance, unless credit control loads their current status from the spreadsheet. Existing customers who are on the spreadsheet stop list today must be on stop in the system from day one.
- **BR-41** Nothing in the new capability should change how existing invoices, statements or postings behave for customers who are not overdue.

### 5.11 Documentation and training

- **BR-42** The staff guide must be updated to explain credit reviews, stop and watch, the reminder run, month-end charges, write-offs and the credit control report.
- **BR-43** Sales staff need a short note on what "watch" and "stop" mean for them and who to contact.

## 6. User Stories

1. **As Maria (credit controller)**, I want to see every Monday which customers are due a review or over their limit, so that I can work through them in order and nothing slips.
2. **As Maria**, I want to put a customer on stop once, and know that the sales office, the web shop, EDI orders and the standing orders are all blocked, so that I don't have to phone round.
3. **As the deputy credit controller**, I want the same powers and the same history as Maria, so that I can cover her holidays without asking her what she agreed with whom.
4. **As a sales rep**, I want to see when one of my customers is on watch or on stop, and why, so that I can talk to the customer before they place an order.
5. **As Maria**, I want the weekly reminder run to email the right letter at the right stage to each overdue customer, after I've had a chance to take out the ones I'm already talking to.
6. **As the Financial Accountant**, I want month-end interest and fees to post themselves to the ledger, so that the debtors control account agrees with the customer balances without manual journals.
7. **As the Finance Director**, I want to approve large write-offs before they go through, so that I know what bad debt we are taking.
8. **As a customer**, I want to see in the portal the reminders and charges on my account, so that I understand what I owe and why.
9. **As the external auditor**, I want to see for any customer who changed their credit limit or status, when and why, so that I can test the credit control process.

## 7. Acceptance Criteria (business terms)

- **AC-01** Maria records a review on a customer, raising their limit and setting next review in six months. The new limit applies straight away, and the review, with her notes, appears in the customer's history. The customer drops off the "due for review" list and reappears when the next date comes round.
- **AC-02** A customer is put on stop. An order for them cannot be completed in the sales office, through the web shop, electronically or from their standing order. When they are taken off stop, orders go through again. Both changes appear in their history with reasons.
- **AC-03** A sales rep tries to take a customer off stop or raise a limit and cannot.
- **AC-04** A customer on watch places an order: it is accepted, the person taking it sees a warning, and the order shows on credit control's list.
- **AC-05** An order that would take a customer over their limit is held and only released when credit control approves it.
- **AC-06** In the reminder run, a customer 35 days overdue gets the first letter by email; the next run, if still unpaid and past the second threshold, they get the second letter; if they pay in between, they get nothing. A customer marked disputed gets no letter. Every letter sent shows on the customer's account history and in their portal.
- **AC-07** At month end, an overdue customer is charged interest at the set rate and the set late fee in their own currency; an exempt customer is not charged; running the charges again for the same month charges nobody twice. The charges appear on the customer's statement and in the portal.
- **AC-08** After month-end charges, waivers and write-offs, the total of customer balances equals the debtors control account in the general ledger.
- **AC-09** A write-off below the approval amount reduces the customer's balance and appears in the bad debt account; one above it does nothing until the Finance Director approves it. The customer is put on stop.
- **AC-10** Rep A sees credit details for her customers and none for Rep B's customers. Customer X in the portal sees only Customer X's reminders and charges.
- **AC-11** After go-live on the live system, all existing customers, balances and history are intact, every customer has a next review date, and everyone on the old spreadsheet stop list is on stop.
- **AC-12** The updated staff guide covers every item in section 4.1 and has been read and agreed by Maria and the Sales Manager.

## 8. Assumptions

- Customers' accounts contact email addresses are mostly up to date; credit control will clean up the rest before go-live.
- Each customer already has a single sales rep assigned.
- Our terms and conditions allow us to charge interest and late fees; Legal will confirm the wording for letters.
- Credit control will provide the current stop list and credit limits from the spreadsheet for go-live.

## 9. Open Questions

1. Interest: a simple annual rate on overdue balances, or a statutory late-payment rate? Does it differ by currency or country?
2. Late fee: one flat fee per month, or a fee per overdue invoice? Should it vary by currency?
3. Do we charge interest on interest and fees that are themselves overdue?
4. Should a customer be put on stop automatically after the final reminder, or only flagged for Maria to decide?
5. How should over-limit orders from the web shop and standing orders be handled: held for approval, or rejected with a message to the customer?
6. What is the approval threshold for write-offs, and does the Financial Accountant also need to sign off?
7. If a written-off debt is later paid, how do we want it shown?
8. Should reps be told the reason for a stop, or only that the customer is on stop?
9. Do we need the reminder letters in languages other than English for overseas customers?
10. Should customers be able to see "watch" status in the portal? (Our view: no.)
11. Who covers credit decisions when both Maria and her deputy are away?
12. Do head-office/branch customer groups share one credit limit, or does each branch have its own?

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.content:
1	# webERP overall system
2	
3	webERP is a PHP and MySQL/MariaDB business application covering sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, finance and reporting. Browser pages and an XML-RPC API read and write one database through `DB_query`. The system hands work to SMTP mail, FTP, the Nominatim geocoder, Dompdf, shell build tools, `composer` and `phpunit`. Work comes in from users, cron URLs, CSV and bank-statement uploads, and EDI files.
4	
5	## Areas
6	
7	- **webERP database installation and upgrade**: creates the database and moves it between versions through three mechanisms:
8	
9	  - the installer's seed data and tables;
10	
11	  - legacy per-version SQL run by `UpgradeDatabase.php`;
12	
13	  - numbered PHP updates run by `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`.
14	
15	  It takes redirects from `includes/session.php`, `includes/GetConfig.php` and the installer wizard. It writes the application tables, `config.DBUpdateNumber` and `config.VersionNumber`.
16	
17	- **webERP finance and ledger area**: the accounting core. It posts receipts, payments, journals, credit notes, depreciation and petty cash into `gltrans`, `banktrans`, `debtortrans` and `supptrans`.
18	
19	  - `gltotals` is kept in step with `gltrans` only by three database triggers. Every GL report reads it, including the trial balance, P&L, balance sheet and account inquiry.
20	
21	  - Apart from update `17.php`, the only code that writes `gltotals` directly is an INSERT in `DateFunctions.php` (line 1221) (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:10-90`, `source/webERP/includes/InstallFunctions.php:735-756`).
22	
23	  - It takes customer and supplier selection and stock and order work from the transactional area, and hands work to PDF and allocation pages.
24	
25	## Cross-area flows
26	
27	1. The installer area's wizard creates the database, folder, config file, tables, triggers and seed data.
28	
29	1. A page request reaches `includes/session.php` or `GetConfig.php`. These redirect to the upgrade area when `DBVersion > DBUpdateNumber` or `VersionNumber` is missing.
30	
31	   - `DBVersion` is the highest available update file. It is worked out once at session start and cached for the rest of the session, so the check compares against that cached value and not against the files on disk. A comment marks this as deliberate (`source/webERP/includes/session.php:272-293`).
32	
33	   - A deployment made while users are logged in does not redirect them. Their sessions run the new code against the old schema, including features that `session.php` gates on `DBUpdateNumber` thresholds, until someone starts a new session and is sent to the upgrade.
34	
35	## Conventions
36	
37	- **GL balance check**: most posting pages call `EnsureGLEntriesBalance`, but at different points.
38	
39	  - Just before the commit: `Credit_Invoice.php`, `SelectCreditItems.php`, `GoodsReceived.php`, `StockAdjustments.php` and the finance receipt batch, among others.
40	
41	  - After the commit: `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php`.
42	
43	  - Mid-transaction: `CounterSales.php`, `CounterReturns.php` and the main supplier posting.
44	
45	  - Not at all: `PDFStockCheckComparison.php` and `WorkOrderCosting.php`.
46	
47	  - Some finance pages keep their own tolerance copies.
48	
49	- **Transactions**: most posting paths show no rollback or error handling, and failed queries are counted or ignored. The exceptions that roll back are the customer allocation pages, the CSV GL import, the customer receipt batch and the legacy upgrade helpers' per-step reporting.
50	
51	- **Upgrade errors**: the legacy runner and the numbered runner both continue after errors.
52	
53	  - **Scope of the guard**: `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` sets the `Errors` counter once per run, not once per file (lines 123-127). The `Errors == 0` guard therefore means "nothing in this run has failed so far", not "this update worked".
54	
55	  - **Effect of a failure**: once any update fails, every later guarded update skips `UpdateDBNo`, even if it succeeded. An unguarded update after that moves `DBUpdateNumber` past all of them (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:121-139`).
56	
57	  - **Reruns**: the next run starts at `DBUpdateNumber`+1 and repeats the updates that already succeeded. This is safe only if they are idempotent. `3.php` is not: it runs a raw `INSERT INTO tags VALUES(0,'None')` and `INSERT INTO gltags SELECT … FROM gltrans`, then `DropColumn('tag','gltrans')`, so a rerun fails once the column is gone (`source/webERP/sql/updates/3.php:3-29`).
58	
59	  - **The rule**: issue #304 set the rule that every update file checks `Errors` before calling `UpdateDBNo`.
60	
61	    - Files 0–16, 25–35 and 43 follow it.
62	
63	    - Files 17–24 and 36–42 call `UpdateDBNo` unconditionally. That is seven of the last eight files, and no comment or script says this was deliberate, so a copy of a recent file will drop the guard (`source/webERP/sql/updates/36.php:4-5`, `source/webERP/sql/updates/42.php:10-11`, `source/webERP/sql/updates/43.php:310-312`).
64	
65	    - `17.php`, `19.php` and `20.php` increment `Errors` themselves and then record the update anyway (`source/webERP/sql/updates/19.php:6-12`).
66	
67	    - The runner has a @todo to move `UpdateDBNo` into the loop, and it has not been done (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:136-137`).
68	
69	## Hazards
70	
71	- Schema changes must be made in four places:
72	
73	  - the update files;
74	
75	  - the install tables and seed data;
76	
77	  - the install triggers in `install/sql/triggers/`;
78	
79	  - the legacy SQL.
80	
81	  Nothing compares them. Fresh installs miss anything added only to an update, and the numbered runner never runs on a fresh install.
82	
83	  - **Unguarded files**: any unguarded file after the failure moves `DBUpdateNumber` past it.
84	
85	  - **Counter reset in `17.php`**: `17.php` sets `$_SESSION['Updates']['Errors']` and `['Successes']` back to 0 partway through a run (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:21-22`). In any run that crosses update 17, the errors from every earlier update in that run are lost.
86	
87	  - **Effect of the reset**: guarded updates after 17 still call `UpdateDBNo`, `DBUpdateNumber` moves past the failed update, and the results screen shows 0 errors for it. This happens even when no unguarded file follows (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:120-158`, `source/webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php:750-755`).
88	
89	- `38.php` calls `CreateTable('auditscript', …)` with SQL that creates `auditscripts` (`source/webERP/sql/updates/38.php:3-16`).
90	
91	  - **Broken existence check**: `CreateTable` checks `SHOW TABLES … ='auditscript'`, which never matches (`source/webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php:518-534`).
92	
93	  - **Reruns fail**: on any rerun the CREATE fails because `auditscripts` already exists. Reruns follow an unrecorded update or a manual `DBUpdateNumber` reset, which is the workaround in issues #311, #760 and #811. The failure raises `Errors`, so every later guarded update in that run (for example 43) does not record.
94	
95	  - **Related names**: the install table file is named `auditscript.sql` but creates `auditscripts` (`source/webERP/install/sql/tables/auditscript.sql:1-9`). `LoginFunctions.php` purges `auditscripts` unconditionally (`source/webERP/includes/LoginFunctions.php:189-192`).
96	
97	- `gltotals` can drift from `gltrans` after update 17.
98	
99	  - **What 17 does**: `17.php` drops the three `gltotals` triggers, rebuilds the totals row by row, recreates the triggers without checking for errors, and records the update unconditionally (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:10-90`).
100	
101	  - **Failed trigger creation**: if `CREATE TRIGGER` fails, for example because the database user lacks the TRIGGER privilege, the upgrade still reports success. From then on, every GL report silently diverges from `gltrans`.
102	
103	  - **Writes during the gap**: any `gltrans` write made between the DROP and the CREATE is also left out of the totals.
104	
105	- Partial postings stay committed.
106	
107	  - Rollback from `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` is followed by autocommit writes, and no caller stops after it.
108	
109	  - Its rounding fix lands on the first row returned, not the largest line.
110

# webERP overall system

webERP is a PHP and MySQL/MariaDB business application covering sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, finance and reporting. Browser pages and an XML-RPC API read and write one database through `DB_query`. The system hands work to SMTP mail, FTP, the Nominatim geocoder, Dompdf, shell build tools, `composer` and `phpunit`. Work comes in from users, cron URLs, CSV and bank-statement uploads, and EDI files.

## Areas

- **webERP database installation and upgrade**: creates the database and moves it between versions through three mechanisms:

  - the installer's seed data and tables;

  - legacy per-version SQL run by `UpgradeDatabase.php`;

  - numbered PHP updates run by `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`.

  It takes redirects from `includes/session.php`, `includes/GetConfig.php` and the installer wizard. It writes the application tables, `config.DBUpdateNumber` and `config.VersionNumber`.

- **webERP finance and ledger area**: the accounting core. It posts receipts, payments, journals, credit notes, depreciation and petty cash into `gltrans`, `banktrans`, `debtortrans` and `supptrans`.

  - `gltotals` is kept in step with `gltrans` only by three database triggers. Every GL report reads it, including the trial balance, P&L, balance sheet and account inquiry.

  - Apart from update `17.php`, the only code that writes `gltotals` directly is an INSERT in `DateFunctions.php` (line 1221) (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:10-90`, `source/webERP/includes/InstallFunctions.php:735-756`).

  - It takes customer and supplier selection and stock and order work from the transactional area, and hands work to PDF and allocation pages.

## Cross-area flows

1. The installer area's wizard creates the database, folder, config file, tables, triggers and seed data.

1. A page request reaches `includes/session.php` or `GetConfig.php`. These redirect to the upgrade area when `DBVersion > DBUpdateNumber` or `VersionNumber` is missing.

   - `DBVersion` is the highest available update file. It is worked out once at session start and cached for the rest of the session, so the check compares against that cached value and not against the files on disk. A comment marks this as deliberate (`source/webERP/includes/session.php:272-293`).

   - A deployment made while users are logged in does not redirect them. Their sessions run the new code against the old schema, including features that `session.php` gates on `DBUpdateNumber` thresholds, until someone starts a new session and is sent to the upgrade.

## Conventions

- **GL balance check**: most posting pages call `EnsureGLEntriesBalance`, but at different points.

  - Just before the commit: `Credit_Invoice.php`, `SelectCreditItems.php`, `GoodsReceived.php`, `StockAdjustments.php` and the finance receipt batch, among others.

  - After the commit: `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php`.

  - Mid-transaction: `CounterSales.php`, `CounterReturns.php` and the main supplier posting.

  - Not at all: `PDFStockCheckComparison.php` and `WorkOrderCosting.php`.

  - Some finance pages keep their own tolerance copies.

- **Transactions**: most posting paths show no rollback or error handling, and failed queries are counted or ignored. The exceptions that roll back are the customer allocation pages, the CSV GL import, the customer receipt batch and the legacy upgrade helpers' per-step reporting.

- **Upgrade errors**: the legacy runner and the numbered runner both continue after errors.

  - **Scope of the guard**: `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` sets the `Errors` counter once per run, not once per file (lines 123-127). The `Errors == 0` guard therefore means "nothing in this run has failed so far", not "this update worked".

  - **Effect of a failure**: once any update fails, every later guarded update skips `UpdateDBNo`, even if it succeeded. An unguarded update after that moves `DBUpdateNumber` past all of them (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:121-139`).

  - **Reruns**: the next run starts at `DBUpdateNumber`+1 and repeats the updates that already succeeded. This is safe only if they are idempotent. `3.php` is not: it runs a raw `INSERT INTO tags VALUES(0,'None')` and `INSERT INTO gltags SELECT … FROM gltrans`, then `DropColumn('tag','gltrans')`, so a rerun fails once the column is gone (`source/webERP/sql/updates/3.php:3-29`).

  - **The rule**: issue #304 set the rule that every update file checks `Errors` before calling `UpdateDBNo`.

    - Files 0–16, 25–35 and 43 follow it.

    - Files 17–24 and 36–42 call `UpdateDBNo` unconditionally. That is seven of the last eight files, and no comment or script says this was deliberate, so a copy of a recent file will drop the guard (`source/webERP/sql/updates/36.php:4-5`, `source/webERP/sql/updates/42.php:10-11`, `source/webERP/sql/updates/43.php:310-312`).

    - `17.php`, `19.php` and `20.php` increment `Errors` themselves and then record the update anyway (`source/webERP/sql/updates/19.php:6-12`).

    - The runner has a @todo to move `UpdateDBNo` into the loop, and it has not been done (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:136-137`).

## Hazards

- Schema changes must be made in four places:

  - the update files;

  - the install tables and seed data;

  - the install triggers in `install/sql/triggers/`;

  - the legacy SQL.

  Nothing compares them. Fresh installs miss anything added only to an update, and the numbered runner never runs on a fresh install.

  - **Unguarded files**: any unguarded file after the failure moves `DBUpdateNumber` past it.

  - **Counter reset in `17.php`**: `17.php` sets `$_SESSION['Updates']['Errors']` and `['Successes']` back to 0 partway through a run (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:21-22`). In any run that crosses update 17, the errors from every earlier update in that run are lost.

  - **Effect of the reset**: guarded updates after 17 still call `UpdateDBNo`, `DBUpdateNumber` moves past the failed update, and the results screen shows 0 errors for it. This happens even when no unguarded file follows (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:120-158`, `source/webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php:750-755`).

- `38.php` calls `CreateTable('auditscript', …)` with SQL that creates `auditscripts` (`source/webERP/sql/updates/38.php:3-16`).

  - **Broken existence check**: `CreateTable` checks `SHOW TABLES … ='auditscript'`, which never matches (`source/webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php:518-534`).

  - **Reruns fail**: on any rerun the CREATE fails because `auditscripts` already exists. Reruns follow an unrecorded update or a manual `DBUpdateNumber` reset, which is the workaround in issues #311, #760 and #811. The failure raises `Errors`, so every later guarded update in that run (for example 43) does not record.

  - **Related names**: the install table file is named `auditscript.sql` but creates `auditscripts` (`source/webERP/install/sql/tables/auditscript.sql:1-9`). `LoginFunctions.php` purges `auditscripts` unconditionally (`source/webERP/includes/LoginFunctions.php:189-192`).

- `gltotals` can drift from `gltrans` after update 17.

  - **What 17 does**: `17.php` drops the three `gltotals` triggers, rebuilds the totals row by row, recreates the triggers without checking for errors, and records the update unconditionally (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:10-90`).

  - **Failed trigger creation**: if `CREATE TRIGGER` fails, for example because the database user lacks the TRIGGER privilege, the upgrade still reports success. From then on, every GL report silently diverges from `gltrans`.

  - **Writes during the gap**: any `gltrans` write made between the DROP and the CREATE is also left out of the totals.

- Partial postings stay committed.

  - Rollback from `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` is followed by autocommit writes, and no caller stops after it.

  - Its rounding fix lands on the first row returned, not the largest line.

- EDI invoices and orders can be resent or duplicated. Enabling `ediinvoices` on an existing customer sends the full history.

- The release and CI checks are weak:

  - The release check validates the previous `demo.sql` and passes when it is missing.

  - `check_syntax.sh` cannot fail the release.

  - `dump_database.sh` truncates the audit trail of the default `weberpdemo` database.

  - CI tests only the Demo=Yes install.

## Children

- [webERP database installation and upgrade](weberp-database-installation-and-upgrade-149/brief.md) — This area covers how a webERP database comes into existence and moves between versions.
- [webERP installer, seed data, schema, build/CI and project-history area](weberp-installer-seed-data-schema-build-ci-and-project-histo-150/brief.md) — This area installs a fresh webERP database and company, supplies the SQL and seed data it loads, and builds, tests and releases the result.
- [webERP: sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, master data, reporting, API…](weberp-sales-purchasing-stock-manufacturing-master-data-repo-151/brief.md) — This area is the webERP PHP application.
- [webERP finance and ledger area](weberp-finance-and-ledger-area-152/brief.md) — This area is the accounting core of webERP.
- [webERP report writer, printable reports and report/admin pages: area overview](weberp-report-writer-printable-reports-and-report-admin-page-153/brief.md) — This area is webERP's reporting and print layer.

2

5	Each numbered PHP file changes the database schema or configuration once. It then records its own number as the latest applied update. The runner `webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` includes the files, and the helper functions in `webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php` (the MySQL/MariaDB variant) do the actual SQL. 8	- **In:** nothing is passed as arguments. Each file runs inside `webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` and uses its helpers and session state: `$_SESSION['Updates']` (`Errors`, `Successes`, `Warnings`, `Messages`) and `$_SESSION['DatabaseName']`.
9	- **Out, config table:** `DBUpdateNumber` is written by `UpdateDBNo`. The `DBUpdateNumber` row is created by 0.php. `VersionNumber` is written by 9.php (`'5.0.0.rc'`) and 31.php (`'5.0.0'`). `ItemDescriptionLanguages` is created by 34.php with value `', '`.

79	  1. Drop the grandchild constraints `stockserialmoves_ibfk_2`, `worequirements_ibfk_3`.
80	  2. Drop the child constraints: `bom_ibfk_1`, `bom_ibfk_2`, `contractbom_ibfk_3`, `custitem_ibfk_1`, `locstock_ibfk_2`, `loctransfers_ibfk_3`, `mrpdemands_ibfk_2`, `offers_ibfk_2`, `orderdeliverydifferenceslog_ibfk_1`, `pickreqdetails_ibfk_1`, `prices_ibfk_1`, `purchdata_ibfk_1`, `recurrsalesorderdetails_ibfk_2`, `salescatprod_ibfk_1`, `salesorderdetails_ibfk_2`, `stockcheckfreeze_ibfk_1`, `stockcounts_ibfk_1`, `stockitemproperties_ibfk_1`, `_ibfk_3`, `_ibfk_5`, `stockmoves_ibfk_1`, `stockrequestitems_ibfk_2`, `_ibfk_4`, `stockserialitems_ibfk_1`, `woitems_ibfk_1`, `worequirements_ibfk_2`.
81	  3. Resize the grandchild columns `stockserialitems.stockid` and `worequirements.stockid`.
82	  4. Resize the child columns: `bom.parent`, `bom.component`, `contractbom.stockid`, `custitem.stockid`, `locstock.stockid`, `loctransfers.stockid`, `mrpdemands.stockid`, `offers.stockid`, `orderdeliverydifferenceslog.stockid`, `pickreqdetails.stockid`, `prices.stockid`, `purchdata.stockid`, `recurrsalesorderdetails.stkcode`, `salescatprod.stockid`, `salesorderdetails.stkcode`, `stockcheckfreeze.stockid`, `stockcounts.stockid`, `stockitemproperties.stockid`, `stockmoves.stockid`, `stockrequestitems.stockid`, `woitems.stockid`.
83	  5. Resize the parent column `stockmaster.stockid`.
84	  6. Re-add the child constraints (the same list as dropped, up to `stockitemproperties_ibfk_5`).
85	  7. Further resizes to VARCHAR(64):
86	     - `stockid` in assetmanager, ediitemmapping, employees, lastcostrollup, loctransfercancellations, pickserialdetails, pricematrix, relateditems, salesanalysis, sellthroughsupport, shipmentcharges, stockdescriptiontranslations, stockserialmoves, supplierdiscounts, tenderitems, woserialnos.
87	     - `relateditems.related`, `lastcostrollup.stockact`, `stockcategory.stockact`, `ediitemmapping.partnerstockid`.
88	     - `purchorderdetails.itemcode`, `grns.itemcode`.
89	     - `worequirements.parentstockid` (its constraint `worequirements_ibfk_3` is dropped and re-added).
90	  8. Constraints are re-added for stockmoves, stockrequestitems (two), stockserialitems, woitems, worequirements, and the `stockserialmoves` compound key (stockid, serialno), including `stockserialmoves_ibfk_2`.
91	  - The condensation lists the grandchild constraints as not re-added in the first block, but the second block says `stockserialmoves_ibfk_2` and `worequirements_ibfk_3` are dropped and re-added after resizing. The sources conflict on whether they come back.
92	  - A TODO notes that `stockitemproperties_ibfk_3` and `_ibfk_5` may be redundant.
93	
94	## Decisions (helper behaviour in `webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php`)
95	- `AddColumn`, `AddCalculatedColumn`: `if DB_table_exists(Table)` and the column is absent (`DB_num_rows == 0`, or `$SQLFile` set) -> ALTER TABLE ADD. Otherwise -> info "already exists". Calculated columns are `STORED`.
96	- `DropColumn`: runs if the column exists or `$SQLFile` is set. Otherwise -> info.
97	- `ChangeColumnSize`: runs only if the current `CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH != $Size`.
98	- `ChangeColumnType`: runs only if `DATA_TYPE` differs.
99	- `ChangeColumnDefault`: runs only if `COLUMN_DEFAULT` differs.
100	- `ChangeColumnName`: runs only if the old column exists and the new one does not.
101	- `NewConfigValue`: INSERT only if the name is absent.
102	- `ChangeConfigValue`: selects `WHERE confvalue = $NewConfigValue`. If no row -> UPDATE, otherwise info.
103	- `DropConstraint`: runs only if `ConstraintExists` is true.
104	- `AddConstraint`: runs only if the constraint is absent. Array fields are imploded.
105	- `DropTable`: runs only if `SHOW TABLES` finds the table.
106	- `executeSQL` result `0` -> success message. Non-zero -> error message with the SQL and error number.
107	- `webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`: `if !isset($_POST['continue'])` -> shows the pending list and a confirmation form. `if isset($_POST['continue'])` -> runs the updates. Range: `$StartingUpdate = $_SESSION['DBUpdateNumber'] + 1` to `$EndingUpdate = $_SESSION['DBVersion']`. `if file_exists('sql/updates/N.php')` -> include it. Foreign key checks are off (`SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0`) while each file runs and on again afterwards.
108	
109	## Order and failure
110	- Each file does its schema change first and records its number last. The record is written only if `Errors == 0`. 19.php and 43.php also guard this way.
111	- 18, 21, 24, 36, 37, 41 and 42 call `UpdateDBNo` unconditionally in the condensations. These files do not show the `Errors == 0` check.
112	- A failing helper reports through `OutputResult` and does not stop the file. Later steps still run.
113	- Nothing is wrapped in a transaction and nothing is rolled back. A failure in a multi-step file (29, 30, 41, 43) leaves the schema partly changed.
114	- `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` collects errors in `$_SESSION['Updates']['Messages']` and carries on to the next numbered update. It then reloads config with `include('includes/GetConfig.php')`.
115	- Loop: `for ($UpdateNumber = $StartingUpdate; $UpdateNumber <= $EndingUpdate; ...)`.
116	
117	## Connections
118	- `webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`: the runner. It includes `sql/updates/N.php`, defines `updateDBNo($NewNumber, $Description)` (`UPDATE config SET confvalue=N WHERE confname='DBUpdateNumber'` and sets `$_SESSION['DBUpdateNumber']`), and defines `executeSQL($SQL, $TrapErrors)`. It initialises `$_SESSION['Updates']` as `Errors 0, Successes 0, Warnings 0`.
119	- `webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php` (and the `_mariadb`, `_mysql`, `_postgres` variants): hold the helpers. The runner includes `includes/UpgradeDB_<DBType>.php`.
120	- `webERP/includes/session.php`:
121	  - Sets `DBVersion = HighestFileName($PathPrefix)`, the highest file in `glob(sql/updates/*.php)`.
122	  - Sets `DBUpdateNumber` to -1 if unset.
123	  - `if DBVersion > DBUpdateNumber` and the page is not `Logout.php` or `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` -> redirect to `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`.
124	  - So adding a new numbered file forces every logged-in session into the upgrade page.
125	- Config table: `DBUpdateNumber`, `VersionNumber`, `ItemDescriptionLanguages`.
126	- Application tables are altered as listed above.
127	
128	## Conclusions
129	- Every file is idempotent through the helper guards, so re-running a file already applied only reports info.
130	- `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` shows no permission check. The only gate is the session redirect from `session.php`.
131	- `session.php` takes the highest file name as the target. The shown set has gaps, such as 1–7, 10, 11, 13, 15–17, 20, 22, 25, 28, 32, 35 and 38–40. Some of these are in other condensations but not in this topic. The runner skips any number whose file does not exist (`file_exists`).
132	- 9.php sets `VersionNumber` to `'5.0.0.rc'` and 31.php later sets `'5.0.0'`.
133	- 36.php shrinks `mrpparameters.location` to 5 characters and 37.php restores it to 50.
134	- 12.php rewrites both `'0000-00-00'` and `'1000-01-01'` end dates to `'9999-12-31'`, which also changes rows that already hold the 1000-01-01 sentinel.
135	- 41.php copies the existing sales exchange-difference account into the new currency account for every company.
136	- 27.php drops constraints that MySQL 8.4+ rejects. 30.php adds the unique key `stockid (stockid, loccode, serialno)` on `stockserialitems` and upgrades the charset. If charset is already utf8mb4 nothing happens for the charset step.
137	- 27.php drops `pickserialdetails_ibfk_2` and 43.php resizes `pickserialdetails.stockid`, but neither re-adds that constraint.
138	- 43.php's drop list leaves `stockitemproperties_ibfk_4` and `_ibfk_6` and `stockrequestitems_ibfk_3` out. 42.php removes those as duplicates.
139

# webERP database migration scripts (`sql/updates/` numbered steps 0–43, partial set)

Part of [webERP database installation and upgrade](weberp-database-installation-and-upgrade-149/brief.md) (path from the export's root): its brief says how work moves through the area and what repairs a failed step.

Each numbered PHP file changes the database schema or configuration once. It then records its own number as the latest applied update. The runner `webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` includes the files, and the helper functions in `webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php` (the MySQL/MariaDB variant) do the actual SQL. Files present here: 0, 8, 9, 12, 14, 18, 19, 21, 23, 24, 26, 27, 29, 30, 31, 33, 34, 36, 37, 41, 42, 43.

## Contract
- **In:** nothing is passed as arguments. Each file runs inside `webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` and uses its helpers and session state: `$_SESSION['Updates']` (`Errors`, `Successes`, `Warnings`, `Messages`) and `$_SESSION['DatabaseName']`.
- **Out, config table:** `DBUpdateNumber` is written by `UpdateDBNo`. The `DBUpdateNumber` row is created by 0.php. `VersionNumber` is written by 9.php (`'5.0.0.rc'`) and 31.php (`'5.0.0'`). `ItemDescriptionLanguages` is created by 34.php with value `', '`.
- **Out, schema:** DDL on the application tables, plus `UPDATE pricematrix` (12.php) and `UPDATE companies` (41.php).
- **Out, messages:** results are reported through `OutputResult` (success, error or info). 30.php also appends to `$_SESSION['Updates']['Messages']`.

## Entry points
Every file runs straight through when included. No file has its own permission check or input check.

- **0.php:** `NewConfigValue('DBUpdateNumber', 0)`. `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo('0', 'Add a new configuration variable to store the latest DB update number')`.
- **8.php:**
  - `DropColumn('actualcost','stockmaster')`.
  - Then `AddCalculatedColumn` for `stockmaster.actualcost` (decimal(20,4), `(materialcost+labourcost+overheadcost)`, after overheadcost).
  - `debtortrans.balance` (double, `(ovamount + ovgst + ovfreight + ovdiscount - alloc)`, after salesperson).
  - `loctransfers.pendingqty` (`(shipqty-recqty)`, after recloc).
  - `salesorderdetails.linenetprice` (`(qtyinvoiced * (unitprice * (1 - discountpercent)))`, after poline).
  - `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo('Create calculated fields to improve speed of access')`.
- **9.php:** `ChangeConfigValue('VersionNumber','5.0.0.rc')`. `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo('Update version number')`.
- **12.php:** `UPDATE pricematrix SET enddate='9999-12-31' WHERE enddate='0000-00-00' OR enddate='1000-01-01'` through `DB_query` with an error message. `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo`.
- **14.php:** `DropColumn('tag','pcexpenses')`, `DropColumn('tag','pcashdetails')`, `DropColumn('defaulttag','pctabs')`. `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo`.
- **18.php:** `ChangeColumnSize('password','emailsettings','VARCHAR(100)',' NOT NULL ','','100')`, then `UpdateDBNo`.
- **19.php:**
  - `ALTER TABLE suppliers MODIFY lastpaiddate DATE`.
  - `if DB_error_no == 0 -> Successes++`, else `Errors++`.
  - Then `UpdateDBNo`.
- **21.php:** `ChangeColumnType('reference','debtortrans','varchar(50)',' NOT NULL ','')`, then `UpdateDBNo`.
- **23.php:** `ChangeColumnDefault(col, table, type, 'NULL', NULL)` for 15 columns, then `UpdateDBNo('Set default to nullable fields')`:

  | Table | Columns |
  |---|---|
  | audittrail | querystring (text) |
  | debtortrans | invtext (text) |
  | glbudgetheaders | description (text) |
  | pcashdetails | purpose (text), receipt (text) |
  | purchorders | comments (longblob) |
  | reportfields | params (text) |
  | salesorders | comments (longblob), internalcomment (blob) |
  | stockdescriptiontranslations | longdescriptiontranslation (text) |
  | stockmoves | narrative (text) |
  | supptrans | transtext (text) |
  | woitems | comments (longblob) |
  | workorders | closecomments (longblob), remark (text) |

- **24.php:** `ChangeColumnType('version','purchorders','DECIMAL(5,2)','NOT NULL','1.00')`, then `UpdateDBNo('Change column type')`.
- **26.php:** `DropTable('tests')`. `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo('Remove unused table')`.
- **27.php:**
  - `DropConstraint('qasamples','qasamples_ibfk_1')`. It referenced `prodspecs.keyval`, which is not unique.
  - `DropConstraint('pickserialdetails','pickserialdetails_ibfk_2')`. It referenced `stockserialitems(stockid, serialno)`, which is not unique.
  - `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo`.
- **29.php:**
  1. Drop `contracts_ibfk_2`, `stockmaster_ibfk_1`, `stockcatproperties_ibfk_1`, `internalstockcatrole_ibfk_1`, `internalstockcatrole_ibfk_3`.
  2. Change `custnotes.noteid` to `int NOT NULL`.
  3. Change `categoryid` to `varchar(6) NOT NULL` in `stockcategory`, `contracts`, `stockmaster`, `stockcatproperties`, `internalstockcatrole`.
  4. Re-add the 5 constraints to `stockcategory.categoryid`.
  5. `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo(29, 'Make column types agree across tables')`.
- **30.php:**
  - Reads the database's `DEFAULT_CHARACTER_SET_NAME` from `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA`.
  - `if $CurrentCharset == 'utf8' || 'utf8mb3' -> ALTER DATABASE ... utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci`. On success it appends the message "Database charset updated to utf8mb4 for MySQL 8.4+ compatibility".
  - `SHOW KEYS FROM stockserialitems WHERE Key_name='stockid'`. `if DB_num_rows == 0 -> ALTER TABLE stockserialitems ADD UNIQUE KEY stockid (stockid, loccode, serialno)`. On success it appends "Added unique key to stockserialitems table".
  - `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo('MySQL 8.4+ utf8mb4 compatibility')`.
- **31.php:** `ChangeConfigValue('VersionNumber','5.0.0')`. `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo('Increment the version number')`.
- **33.php:** `AddCalculatedColumn('balance','supptrans','double','NOT NULL','(ovamount + ovgst - alloc)','id')`. `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo('Create calculated fields to improve speed of access')`.
- **34.php:** `NewConfigValue('ItemDescriptionLanguages', ', ')`. `if Errors == 0 -> UpdateDBNo('Create config value for multi languages')`.
- **36.php:** `ChangeColumnSize('location','mrpparameters','VARCHAR(5)',' NULL ','','5')`, then `UpdateDBNo`.
- **37.php:** `ChangeColumnSize('location','mrpparameters','VARCHAR(50)',' NULL ','','50')`, then `UpdateDBNo('Update back the size of the location field in mrpparameters to 50 chars')`.
- **41.php:**
  1. `ChangeColumnName('exchangediffact','companies','varchar(20)','NOT NULL','65000','salesexchangediffact','')`.
  2. `AddColumn('currencyexchangediffact','companies','varchar(20)','NOT NULL','65000','purchasesexchangediffact')`.
  3. `executeSQL("UPDATE companies SET currencyexchangediffact = salesexchangediffact")`.
  4. `UpdateDBNo('Add Currency Exchange Rate Difference GL Account')`.
- **42.php:** drops `stockitemproperties_ibfk_3`, `_ibfk_4`, `_ibfk_5`, `_ibfk_6`, `stockrequestitems_ibfk_3`, `_ibfk_4`. Then `UpdateDBNo('Drop duplicate foreign keys')`.
- **43.php:** widens `stockmaster.stockid` from VARCHAR(20) to VARCHAR(64) and `stockmaster.description` to VARCHAR(255). `UpdateDBNo('Increase stockmaster.stockid and description size')` runs only if `Errors == 0`. Order:
  1. Drop the grandchild constraints `stockserialmoves_ibfk_2`, `worequirements_ibfk_3`.
  2. Drop the child constraints: `bom_ibfk_1`, `bom_ibfk_2`, `contractbom_ibfk_3`, `custitem_ibfk_1`, `locstock_ibfk_2`, `loctransfers_ibfk_3`, `mrpdemands_ibfk_2`, `offers_ibfk_2`, `orderdeliverydifferenceslog_ibfk_1`, `pickreqdetails_ibfk_1`, `prices_ibfk_1`, `purchdata_ibfk_1`, `recurrsalesorderdetails_ibfk_2`, `salescatprod_ibfk_1`, `salesorderdetails_ibfk_2`, `stockcheckfreeze_ibfk_1`, `stockcounts_ibfk_1`, `stockitemproperties_ibfk_1`, `_ibfk_3`, `_ibfk_5`, `stockmoves_ibfk_1`, `stockrequestitems_ibfk_2`, `_ibfk_4`, `stockserialitems_ibfk_1`, `woitems_ibfk_1`, `worequirements_ibfk_2`.
  3. Resize the grandchild columns `stockserialitems.stockid` and `worequirements.stockid`.
  4. Resize the child columns: `bom.parent`, `bom.component`, `contractbom.stockid`, `custitem.stockid`, `locstock.stockid`, `loctransfers.stockid`, `mrpdemands.stockid`, `offers.stockid`, `orderdeliverydifferenceslog.stockid`, `pickreqdetails.stockid`, `prices.stockid`, `purchdata.stockid`, `recurrsalesorderdetails.stkcode`, `salescatprod.stockid`, `salesorderdetails.stkcode`, `stockcheckfreeze.stockid`, `stockcounts.stockid`, `stockitemproperties.stockid`, `stockmoves.stockid`, `stockrequestitems.stockid`, `woitems.stockid`.
  5. Resize the parent column `stockmaster.stockid`.
  6. Re-add the child constraints (the same list as dropped, up to `stockitemproperties_ibfk_5`).
  7. Further resizes to VARCHAR(64):
     - `stockid` in assetmanager, ediitemmapping, employees, lastcostrollup, loctransfercancellations, pickserialdetails, pricematrix, relateditems, salesanalysis, sellthroughsupport, shipmentcharges, stockdescriptiontranslations, stockserialmoves, supplierdiscounts, tenderitems, woserialnos.
     - `relateditems.related`, `lastcostrollup.stockact`, `stockcategory.stockact`, `ediitemmapping.partnerstockid`.
     - `purchorderdetails.itemcode`, `grns.itemcode`.
     - `worequirements.parentstockid` (its constraint `worequirements_ibfk_3` is dropped and re-added).
  8. Constraints are re-added for stockmoves, stockrequestitems (two), stockserialitems, woitems, worequirements, and the `stockserialmoves` compound key (stockid, serialno), including `stockserialmoves_ibfk_2`.
  - The condensation lists the grandchild constraints as not re-added in the first block, but the second block says `stockserialmoves_ibfk_2` and `worequirements_ibfk_3` are dropped and re-added after resizing. The sources conflict on whether they come back.
  - A TODO notes that `stockitemproperties_ibfk_3` and `_ibfk_5` may be redundant.

## Decisions (helper behaviour in `webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php`)
- `AddColumn`, `AddCalculatedColumn`: `if DB_table_exists(Table)` and the column is absent (`DB_num_rows == 0`, or `$SQLFile` set) -> ALTER TABLE ADD. Otherwise -> info "already exists". Calculated columns are `STORED`.
- `DropColumn`: runs if the column exists or `$SQLFile` is set. Otherwise -> info.
- `ChangeColumnSize`: runs only if the current `CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH != $Size`.
- `ChangeColumnType`: runs only if `DATA_TYPE` differs.
- `ChangeColumnDefault`: runs only if `COLUMN_DEFAULT` differs.
- `ChangeColumnName`: runs only if the old column exists and the new one does not.
- `NewConfigValue`: INSERT only if the name is absent.
- `ChangeConfigValue`: selects `WHERE confvalue = $NewConfigValue`. If no row -> UPDATE, otherwise info.
- `DropConstraint`: runs only if `ConstraintExists` is true.
- `AddConstraint`: runs only if the constraint is absent. Array fields are imploded.
- `DropTable`: runs only if `SHOW TABLES` finds the table.
- `executeSQL` result `0` -> success message. Non-zero -> error message with the SQL and error number.
- `webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`: `if !isset($_POST['continue'])` -> shows the pending list and a confirmation form. `if isset($_POST['continue'])` -> runs the updates. Range: `$StartingUpdate = $_SESSION['DBUpdateNumber'] + 1` to `$EndingUpdate = $_SESSION['DBVersion']`. `if file_exists('sql/updates/N.php')` -> include it. Foreign key checks are off (`SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0`) while each file runs and on again afterwards.

## Order and failure
- Each file does its schema change first and records its number last. The record is written only if `Errors == 0`. 19.php and 43.php also guard this way.
- 18, 21, 24, 36, 37, 41 and 42 call `UpdateDBNo` unconditionally in the condensations. These files do not show the `Errors == 0` check.
- A failing helper reports through `OutputResult` and does not stop the file. Later steps still run.
- Nothing is wrapped in a transaction and nothing is rolled back. A failure in a multi-step file (29, 30, 41, 43) leaves the schema partly changed.
- `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` collects errors in `$_SESSION['Updates']['Messages']` and carries on to the next numbered update. It then reloads config with `include('includes/GetConfig.php')`.
- Loop: `for ($UpdateNumber = $StartingUpdate; $UpdateNumber <= $EndingUpdate; ...)`.

## Connections
- `webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`: the runner. It includes `sql/updates/N.php`, defines `updateDBNo($NewNumber, $Description)` (`UPDATE config SET confvalue=N WHERE confname='DBUpdateNumber'` and sets `$_SESSION['DBUpdateNumber']`), and defines `executeSQL($SQL, $TrapErrors)`. It initialises `$_SESSION['Updates']` as `Errors 0, Successes 0, Warnings 0`.
- `webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php` (and the `_mariadb`, `_mysql`, `_postgres` variants): hold the helpers. The runner includes `includes/UpgradeDB_<DBType>.php`.
- `webERP/includes/session.php`:
  - Sets `DBVersion = HighestFileName($PathPrefix)`, the highest file in `glob(sql/updates/*.php)`.
  - Sets `DBUpdateNumber` to -1 if unset.
  - `if DBVersion > DBUpdateNumber` and the page is not `Logout.php` or `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` -> redirect to `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`.
  - So adding a new numbered file forces every logged-in session into the upgrade page.
- Config table: `DBUpdateNumber`, `VersionNumber`, `ItemDescriptionLanguages`.
- Application tables are altered as listed above.

## Conclusions
- Every file is idempotent through the helper guards, so re-running a file already applied only reports info.
- `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` shows no permission check. The only gate is the session redirect from `session.php`.
- `session.php` takes the highest file name as the target. The shown set has gaps, such as 1–7, 10, 11, 13, 15–17, 20, 22, 25, 28, 32, 35 and 38–40. Some of these are in other condensations but not in this topic. The runner skips any number whose file does not exist (`file_exists`).
- 9.php sets `VersionNumber` to `'5.0.0.rc'` and 31.php later sets `'5.0.0'`.
- 36.php shrinks `mrpparameters.location` to 5 characters and 37.php restores it to 50.
- 12.php rewrites both `'0000-00-00'` and `'1000-01-01'` end dates to `'9999-12-31'`, which also changes rows that already hold the 1000-01-01 sentinel.
- 41.php copies the existing sales exchange-difference account into the new currency account for every company.
- 27.php drops constraints that MySQL 8.4+ rejects. 30.php adds the unique key `stockid (stockid, loccode, serialno)` on `stockserialitems` and upgrades the charset. If charset is already utf8mb4 nothing happens for the charset step.
- 27.php drops `pickserialdetails_ibfk_2` and 43.php resizes `pickserialdetails.stockid`, but neither re-adds that constraint.
- 43.php's drop list leaves `stockitemproperties_ibfk_4` and `_ibfk_6` and `stockrequestitems_ibfk_3` out. 42.php removes those as duplicates.

## Hazards
- No transactions or rollbacks. The 43.php chain of drop, resize and re-add can leave foreign keys missing if it fails midway.
- 12.php, 14.php, 18.php, 19.php, 21.php, 24.php, 33.php and 36.php have no failure handler beyond `OutputResult`.
- 29.php does not check that existing `categoryid` data fits `varchar(6)`.
- SQL is built by string concatenation with no escaping in the helpers.
- 19.php counts `Successes` and `Errors` itself, but other files rely on the helpers to do so. The helper condensation shows only `OutputResult` and does not show them incrementing `Errors`. If they never do, the `Errors == 0` guard never blocks `UpdateDBNo`.

5	Each page in this topic is a standalone PHP page. It maintains one reference table, or runs an administrative clean-up (the `Z_` scripts). Each page reads and writes the database directly through `DB_query`, and the user reaches it from a menu. None of them is handed work by another part in code. The only link out to another page is the SalesPeople.php link to `SalesCommissionRates.php`.

7	## Contract
8	- **Input.** Every page takes browser GET and POST parameters. Common ones are a `Selected…` key, `submit` or `Submit`, `delete` and `FormID`. Per-page fields are listed under Entry points.
9	- **Output.** Each page writes SQL to the webERP database and renders HTML. Results are shown with `prnMsg($Msg, $Type)`, which is defined in webERP/includes/MiscFunctions.php. It appends `array($Msg,$Type,$Prefix)` to the global `$Messages`, and only returns a div when `$Return` is true.
10	- **Config.** CustomerTypes.php, SalesTypes.php and SupplierTypes.php write the `config` table rows `DefaultCustomerType`, `DefaultPriceList` and `DefaultSupplierType`. Shippers.php reads `$_SESSION['Default_Shipper']`. Session config is loaded from the `config` table by webERP/includes/GetConfig.php.
11	- **Link out.** SalesPeople.php links to `SalesCommissionRates.php?SelectedSalesPerson=urlencode(salesmancode)`.
12	- **Menu.** Most pages are listed in webERP/install/sql/data/menuitems.sql, under these menu groups:

16	| system/Reports | SalesTypes, SupplierTypes, CustomerTypes, CreditStatus, PaymentMethods, Areas, SalesPeople, Shippers, SalesCommissionTypes |
